milestones.name: A change that breaks a test behind a Cargo feature fails its merge's check, and those tests run on main after each merge
milestones.quality_bar: As dependable as the feature matrix of a well-kept Rust workspace such as wgpu's or Bevy's: no test sits behind a feature that nothing builds, and anyone can see from one list where each such test runs.

items.statement: `./dev check` builds and lints every test that sits behind a Cargo feature, with that feature on: the test targets of each package the main-tier list names, with the features the list gives it, under the lints the rest of the workspace gets. That is `thrum-render` with `creation-counters`, the game with `draw-probe` and `thrum-asset-gpu/fault-probe`, and `thrum-asset-gpu` with its own `draw-probe`. The record gives what the step adds to the check's time.
items.ask: In a scratch copy, add a type error to `crates/thrum-render/tests/ray_instances_seam.rs`; separately to `examples/v1-game/tests/cooked_fault_gpu.rs`; and separately inside the `draw-probe` test of `crates/thrum-asset-gpu/tests/error_types.rs`: does `./dev check` fail on each? Does the step take its packages and features from the list, with no second copy of them in the command? What did the step add to the check's time on a warm build, measured, with the load recorded?

items.statement: `./dev long-tests` also runs every test behind a Cargo feature, with its feature on and a GPU required, and they pass in the main-branch check `long-tests` on main at the claimed commit. The main-tier list names each package with its features, and covers it whole or by test binary: `thrum-render` is listed whole with `creation-counters`, so every test binary of that package runs with the feature on and a new one runs with no edit to the list. A test that failed at the starting commit is listed as not run, with its failure and the module that owns it, and is not changed.
items.ask: Search the workspace's test files and manifests for a Cargo feature, in `required-features` and in `cfg`: is each test it gates covered by the list with that feature, or listed as not run with its failure and its owner? Was any such test edited? Does the handoff name each test listed as not run? How long does one run of `./dev long-tests` take now, and is the settings line's timeout at least twice that?

items.statement: A Cargo feature cannot take a test out of every tier unnoticed, however the test is gated. `./dev check-docs` fails when a test target requires a feature, or a `cfg` in a test file names one, and the main-tier list does not cover that file's package with that feature: whole, or by the test binary the file builds into. The message names the file, the feature and the list.
items.ask: In a scratch copy, add `crates/thrum-render/tests/zz_probe_gpu.rs` holding one test under `#[cfg(feature = "creation-counters")]`: does `./dev check-docs` pass, and is that binary among what `./dev long-tests` runs for `thrum-render`, with no edit to the list? milestones.name: A merge's check runs only the tests of the packages its change can reach, and the whole workspace's tests run on main after each merge
milestones.quality_bar: As trustworthy as change-based test selection in a well-kept Rust workspace, such as cargo-nextest's reverse-dependency filters or the determinator the guppy project built for Diem's CI: the selection follows Cargo's own graph, anything it cannot place runs everything, and the saving is measured before it is relied on.

items.statement: Before the selection is switched on, the record gives what it saves. For each landing on main over at least the week before the starting commit it gives the packages the selection as built picks and the time their test binaries take against the whole workspace's, from per-binary times measured at that commit. It gives the mean saving and the share of landings that run the whole workspace, and one timed pair on this Mac with the load recorded: `./dev check` for a change to one package nothing depends on, against the whole-workspace run.
items.ask: Does the record replay real landings through the selection as built, with per-binary times from a run at the starting commit? What is the mean saving, and what share of landings run the whole workspace? Does the log show the record was made before the selection was switched on?

items.statement: `./dev check` runs the unit and integration test binaries of the packages its change can reach and of no other: each workspace package that holds a changed path, every workspace package that depends on one, directly or through others, as a normal, build or dev dependency, and the package a declared edge names for a changed path. The change is every path that differs between the checkout and its merge base with the main branch, uncommitted and untracked paths included. The build, the lints, the repository guards, the script suites and the doc tests run whole, as they did, and the draw-probe pass of the cooked-asset tests runs when the game's package is selected. The check prints what it selected and why.
items.check: sh -c 'out=$(cargo test --locked --offline -p xtask selection 2>&1) && echo "$out" | grep -qE "test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed"'
items.ask: Read the selection's tests: do they cover a file of a package nothing depends on, a file of a package others depend on, an edge that is only a dev dependency, and an uncommitted file? In a scratch branch that changes one source file of `thrum-rain-model`, which test binaries does `./dev check` run, and does it still lint the whole workspace? In one that changes `thrum-core`?

items.statement: Where the selection cannot be sure, `./dev check` runs the whole workspace's tests and says why. That is so for a change to the root manifest, the lockfile, the toolchain file, the lint configuration, `./dev` itself, `tools/xtask` or the test runner's own configuration; for a changed path the design gives no rule; and for a checkout with no merge base, with no difference from the main branch, or with a dependency graph the check cannot read. Markdown, `docs/` outside `docs/evidence`, the plans, `.agents/`, `.github/`, `scripts/` and the data under `.config/` that only the guards read select no Rust test.
items.ask: Read the path rules and their tests: is every rule of the design there, and does a path with no rule select everything? In scratch branches, change only `Cargo.lock`; only `rust-toolchain.toml`; add a file in a new top-level folder; and check out main's tip with nothing changed: does each run the whole workspace and say why? Does a branch that changes only a Markdown file and a script run no Rust test binary, and still run the guards and script suites?

items.statement: A test that reads another package's files when it runs is selected when those files change. A declared edge, kept and tested with the path rules, names a path and the package whose own test binaries a change under it selects as well. `crates/thrum-asset-gpu/src/` selects `thrum-render`, whose guard on where cooked pipelines are created scans that folder. No test code reads a tracked file outside its own package except through a dependency of its package, a declared edge, or a path that selects the whole workspace.
items.ask: In a scratch branch that changes only one file under `crates/thrum-asset-gpu/src/`, does `./dev check` run `every_cooked_pipeline_goes_through_the_seam_and_escapes_nothing`, and say that a declared edge selected `thrum-render`? Does it leave out the packages that depend on `thrum-render` and not on `thrum-asset-gpu`? Search test code for a reader outside its own package: `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` joined with a path that climbs out of the package, and `include_str!`, `include_bytes!` or `#[path]` that does. Is each one a dependency of the reader's package, a declared edge, a path that selects everything, or scratch under `tmp/`?

items.statement: A selected test binary is the binary the whole-workspace run executes: the check builds the workspace's test binaries once, with the workspace's features, and the selection decides only which of them run.
items.ask: For two packages, compare the test binary a selected run executes with the one `./dev check-all` executes on the same commit: is it the same file? Does a selected run compile any crate that a whole-workspace run on the same commit had already built?

items.statement: `./dev check-all` runs everything `./dev check` ran before this milestone, the whole workspace's tests included, whatever changed. `./dev help` lists it, and `ORCHESTRATE.md` declares the main-branch check `workspace-tests` in the design's words, with the timeout set as the design says.
items.check: sh -c './dev help | grep -q check-all && grep -q "Main-branch check workspace-tests:" ORCHESTRATE.md'
items.ask: Compare the steps of `./dev check-all` with the steps of `./dev check` at the starting commit: is any step or test binary missing? Is the settings line the design's, word for word but for the timeout?

items.statement: The whole workspace's tests pass in the main-branch check `workspace-tests`, on main at the claimed commit.

`./dev check` and `./dev check-all` fail when one test binary's run takes over the limit by the check's own clock. The limit is three minutes, or twice the time the slowest binary the check keeps took while the main-branch check `long-tests` was running, where that time is over 90 seconds; the record gives that time and the log gives the limit. The message names the binary and says what to do: make the test fast, or mark it `#[ignore]` with a reason that starts `long:` and list it. The foam scene's binary is exempt by name until M3, and no other binary is.

Is any binary exempt but the foam scene's? Does the record give the slowest kept binary's time from a check that overlapped a run of the main-branch check `long-tests`, and is the limit at least twice it?

milestones.name: The check builds and runs its tests the fastest way a measurement supports, and the record says how long a merge's check and the main tier take now
milestones.quality_bar: As measured as a build-profile change in a well-kept Rust workspace such as Bevy's or wgpu's: timed both ways on one commit before it is switched on, with the same tests passing after as before.

items.statement: The record times the whole-workspace run, `./dev check-all`, on one commit three ways: as it is; with dependencies optimised in test builds; and with test binaries run by nextest, GPU tests held to two at once. Each way is run twice, alternating, and each run has its wall time, the load average and what else was running.
items.ask: Does the record hold two runs of each of the three arrangements on one commit, alternated and not grouped, each with its load? Is the build time of a changed profile counted in its runs or stated beside them?

items.statement: An arrangement is on only if both of its runs were shorter than both runs of the whole-workspace run as it was. Where both are on, the run that gives the time afterwards is shorter than both of those runs too, or the arrangement that won by less is off. One that did not win is left out, and the record says so. Test builds keep debug assertions and overflow checks. Where nextest is on, a machine without it still runs every test through `cargo test`, doc tests still run, tests that share a device through an in-process lock run one at a time, the merge check still runs only the tests of the packages its change can reach, on binaries built for the whole workspace, and a test or binary over the limit still fails the check.
items.ask: Read the record and the diff. Is each arrangement that is on one that won both ways, and if two are on, did the pair beat the run as it was? Do test builds keep debug assertions and overflow checks? If nextest is on: what runs where it is not installed, do doc tests run, are the files that guard GPU residency or device loss with a mutex held to one test at a time, does a scratch change to one leaf package still run only that package's tests, and does a slow test still fail the check?

items.statement: Every test that ran and passed in the whole-workspace run before this milestone still runs and passes in it on this Mac, and none is skipped; a test the check ran twice may now run once. The record holds the test results before and after, the later run made with `THRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1`.
items.ask: Compare the two recorded runs test by test, not their totals: does every test that reported ok before report ok after, at least once? Does the later run hold any `thrum-gpu-skip:` line?

items.statement: `./dev check` runs each cooked-asset test once against the production build, in the workspace pass, and its draw-probe pass runs only the tests that assert on the draw probe.
items.ask: Which tests of the cooked-assets binary read the draw probe? Does the probe pass run each of them and no other test of that binary, and does the workspace pass still run all of them?

items.statement: The record gives a merge's check time at this module's start, as the design records it, and now, for a change to one leaf package and for the whole workspace, and how long one run of `./dev long-tests` takes, each on this Mac with the load recorded. `CONTRIBUTING.md` says what `./dev check` runs and how it selects, what `./dev check-all` and `./dev long-tests` run on main after the merge, and how to run one long test by hand.
items.ask: Do the record's times for the check and for the long tests come from runs at the claimed commit, each with its load? Does `CONTRIBUTING.md` name the three commands, say what selects a merge's tests, and say how to run one long test by hand?
